name:
Example: 
                    Identifying Points that Must Lie on a Translated Curve
problem: The point $P$ with coordinates $(3,4)$ lies on the curve $y=f(x)$. Find a point that must lie on $y=f(x)+3$?
worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The graph of $y = f(x)+3$ is obtained by translating the graph of $y=f(x)$ by $3$ units *up*. 

Hence, if the point $(3,4)$ lies on $y=f(x)$, then the point 

$$
(3,4+3) = (3,7)
$$

lies on $y=f(x) + 3.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14218283/assets/577911187229d6a56a8885e4cea2e25752615ed7bb807768abf4b54c5073d177.png)

**Method 2**

As $(3,4)$ lies on $y = f(x)$, we have that $f(3) = 4.$

Now, if $x = 3$ then

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =f(3)+3 \\  & =4+3 \\  & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the point $(3,7)$ must lie on $y = f(x) + 3.$
